condition.notes: Desktop main rails (3V3/5V/12V) missing. These only come up after the motherboard pulls PS_ON# (pin 16, green wire) low. If PS_ON# is high, the PSU is correctly keeping the main rails off.

next_steps.action: Measure PS_ON# (pin 16 of the 24-pin ATX, green wire) relative to ground. Then briefly short PS_ON# to ground with a jumper (or press the front-panel power button) and re-measure the missing rail.

measure.what: PS_ON# voltage and the missing rail's response to PS_ON# being pulled low
measure.where: Pin 16 of the 24-pin ATX (green wire); the missing rail test point
measure.expected: PS_ON# is HIGH (>2 V, pulled up to 5VSB by the PSU) when the system is off. It goes LOW (<0.4 V) when the front-panel button is pressed. When PS_ON# is low, all main rails should come up within 100-500 ms.
measure.safety: Shorting PS_ON# to ground is safe — it is a logic input with a pull-up. NEVER short any other pin of the ATX connector to ground.

interpretations.if_result: PS_ON# goes low and the rail comes up
interpretations.then: The PSU and the rail are good. The fault is in the front-panel button, the super-IO, or the EC that drives PS_ON#.

interpretations.if_result: PS_ON# goes low but the rail still missing
interpretations.then: PSU is not turning on the rail. Suspect a PSU fault or a short on the rail holding it down. Measure the rail resistance again; if low, hunt the short. If resistance is normal, replace the PSU.

interpretations.if_result: PS_ON# stays high when the button is pressed
interpretations.then: Motherboard is not asserting PS_ON#. Could be: dead 5VSB (check ATX_5VSB first), dead super-IO/EC, stuck power button, or a stuck PWR_OK from a previous cycle. Diagnose the 5VSB and super-IO first.
